DEBUG is set to True in production settings. When DEBUG is enabled, Django exposes detailed error pages with stack traces, settings values, and system information that can aid attackers in reconnaissance and exploitation.

The SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in the settings file with a predictable value. This key is used for cryptographic signing in Django (sessions, password reset tokens, messages). If exposed, attackers can forge sessions, bypass authentication, and perform other attacks.

The CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, which disables Django's built-in CSRF protection across the entire application. This makes all state-changing operations vulnerable to CSRF attacks unless individual views implement their own protection.

The show_toolbar function enables the Django Debug Toolbar when 'debug' is present in GET, POST, or cookies. Combined with DEBUG=True, this exposes sensitive information including SQL queries, settings, and request data to anyone who adds ?debug=1 to any URL.

The boom function intentionally raises an unhandled exception. When DEBUG=True (as configured in settings.py), this exposes detailed stack traces with file paths, code snippets, and system information to the end user, aiding attackers in reconnaissance.
